human_tolerance.notes: Uses residential areas as well as woodland edges and dense shrub cover. Garden use is an inference from its documented use of residential habitat.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: US Forest Service review: breeding spans late April to mid-August; peak mid-May to mid-June. Dates summarize a broad US population and do not imply each state has identical timing.

phases.name: dispersal
phases.note: Southward migration begins early in fall after young leave the nest. This broad US interval is a seasonal summary, not a state-specific departure date.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Spring migration and arrival on breeding grounds; males arrive before females.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Nationally scoped proxy: many northern US breeding birds leave for the south, while catbirds also winter in the southern US. This cannot describe the state-level north/south split; the US-wide absent marker can overstate winter absence locally and must be revisited if state-scoped presence is added.

vocalizations.description: A long, raspy, irregular sequence of phrases; most phrases are sung once, and birds sometimes imitate other sounds.
A nasal, cat-like mewing call that gives the species its common name.
A quiet alarm call described as resembling the calls of a male mallard.

taxonomy.note: GBIF match returned accepted species rank (confidence 99); USFS review uses the same accepted scientific name and family.

range.native.note: The review lists the species as native in the United States; this record supports the requested US activity region.

traits.body_plan.note: Bird morphology and taxonomy identify a feathered, bipedal vertebrate.

traits.limb_count.note: Bird schema convention counts legs, not wings.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Ground foraging with hops and short low flights between vegetation.

traits.nest_type.note: The species builds a cup nest in shrubs and low trees.

traits.size_class.note: Small: mass 0.0375 kg is below 1 kg.

traits.mass_kg.note: 0.0375 kg converts the published 35–40 g average range to its midpoint (37.5 g).

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Published adult range 23.2–56.5 g converted to kg by dividing by 1000.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 20.5–24 cm range, converted to metres.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 22–30 cm range, converted to metres.

traits.lifespan_y.note: USFS review reports average longevity around 2.5 years; the source summary does not establish sampling scope, so this is a low-confidence proxy for typical wild lifespan.

traits.diet.note: USFS says about half insects and most remainder fleshy shrub fruit; percentages are normalized to 0.5 each as a coarse simulation allocation, not a measured exact split.

traits.social.note: Solitary group size is a simulation judgement; source describes territorial pairs during breeding but does not establish typical nonbreeding group size.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Daytime song and foraging; migration at night does not change the daily activity classification.

traits.defense.note: Flee models ordinary threat response. At nests catbirds may mob predators, a behavior the current action vocabulary cannot represent.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.45. Species uses residential habitats but relies on dense cover; no measured approach distance was found.

habitat.use.note: Judgement: 0.55 ground and 0.45 shrub/low-tree use; literature describes ground leaf-litter foraging and shrub/tree nesting and foraging, but gives no time budget.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Dense shrubs and vines provide cover.

habitat.resources.note: Diet weights follow the approximate half insect/half fruit allocation. Food months and resource importance are authored model simplifications from spring-summer insect feeding and late-summer/fall fruit use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapter and garden use are inferred from documented residential/urban/suburban habitat use; this is not evidence of dependence on gardens.

seasonal.strategy.note: The review describes spring arrival, early-fall southbound migration and winter range in the southern US and farther south.

seasonal.phases.note: Broad US season summary; the review describes breeding from late April to mid-August, spring arrival before breeding and southbound migration beginning early fall.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Review describes eggs, nestlings/fledglings and sexually mature adults; duration omitted where no single typical value was selected.

behavior.note: Authored to represent alarm and short flight between cover, perching, low hop-foraging, shrub nesting in April-August, and both diet categories. Nest defense by mobbing remains unsupported by the behavior action set.

vocalizations.note: Song, mimicking, mewing name-call, and alarm-call description.

look.note: Judgement in the block model: slate gray body, darker cap and tail, rust undertail coverts. Proportions and box dimensions are authored approximation, not measured anatomy.

external.note: Provider-specific identifiers independently resolved: GBIF match accepted species key 2494936; iNaturalist active species taxon 14995. The iNaturalist source supports only its own identifier and has a non-commercial licence because no other source can verify that provider-specific key.

range.note: The USFS review identifies the species as native in the United States.
